_comment_family: The family name here is one this app invents. The file is a VARIABLE
font: it calls itself 'Scale VF' and carries a whole family along two
axes, from ExtraCondensed ExtraLight to SuperExtended Black. Asked for
by its own name it hands back its default instance — the Regular at
normal width — which is not the cut anything is designed in.
Registering it under the name of the instance we want, pinned to that
instance by the descriptors below, is what makes 'Scale VF Condensed
Bold' a face the canvas can simply ask for. A second channel wanting a
different cut of the same file declares its own pack the same way;
they are separate faces to the browser and do not collide.
_comment_pinning: wght 700 and wdth 75 — the file's own 'Condensed Bold' instance.
A single-valued descriptor is a clamp, not a filter: whatever weight or
width the canvas asks for is pulled into the range declared here, and
with the range one value wide the face can only be drawn at that
instance. `stretch` is what does the work — canvas takes no
font-stretch, so 75% could not be asked for at the point of drawing
even if we wanted to. `variationSettings` states the same instance
straight to the axes, so the cut survives a browser whose font matching
ever stops clamping. Measured here: 920.5px for the probe string
against 846.2 at wght 400 and 1182.9 at wdth 100, so both axes land.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css: this face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON, which is the route content/README.md
describes. It also has to be — the pinning above lives in the FontFace
descriptors, and there is no stylesheet rule for it to inherit.
_comment_local: Deliberately empty. A local() source resolves by NAME, and no font
installed on any machine is called 'Scale VF Condensed Bold' — the
name only exists because of the registration above. Anything Windows
handed back under a name close to it would be some other cut of the
family at best, so the file is the only route, and a missing file is
reported as missing rather than quietly replaced.
